Subsequently, all at once, every element appeared to align—Wexcombe, professors, classes, students, studies, and social activities. The Freshmen, no longer an assemblage of disconnected people, realized they were a class, possessing a class spirit, a class yell, class interests, class antipathies, and class ambitions. Victory belonged to them in the yearly “Arts Rush” against the Sophomores, through which they acquired the esteem of every class, alongside a huge, confidence-instilling self-image. Furthermore, he received an invitation to enter the “Lambs”—Redmondese denoting Lamba Theta—an honor seldom offered to a Freshman. passages.v03:c03:p0000: Wilfred Mott, Hugh Carrow, and Nell Harcourt departed from Brierley on the subsequent Monday morning. Nell had wished that the day would be fine. Isolde was scheduled to chauffeur her to the station, and the two desired that this drive, which would be their final one together for a while, might prove enjoyable. However, as Nell retired to bed on Sunday evening, the east wind was lamenting about Grey Shutters with a menacing prediction that came to pass when morning arrived. Upon waking, Nell discovered raindrops tapping against her windowpane and creating expanding circles on the gray face of the pond; fog concealed the hills and the sea, making the entire world appear dark and dismal. Nell put on her clothes in the gloomy gray twilight of dawn, since setting out early was required to make the connection for the boat train; she fought against tears that kept rising to her eyes regardless of her efforts. She was departing from the home she held so precious, and an inner feeling suggested that her departure was permanent, except for visits as a vacation retreat. Circumstances would never return to what they had been; returning for holidays would not constitute residing there. And oh, how cherished and adored every single detail was—that small white porch room, dedicated to the daydreams of her youth, the ancient Frost Maiden by the window, the stream down in the hollow, the Nymph’s Well, the Haunted Woods, and Linger Lane—every one of the countless beloved places where recollections of former years lingered. Was it possible for her to ever experience true happiness in any other place?
passages.v03:c03:p0002: Punctually at the appointed hour Isolde arrived with horse and buggy, her flushed countenance shining over her raincoat. At that point, the farewells somehow needed to be spoken. Entering from her quarters, Mrs. Sowerby warmly hugged Nell and cautioned her to take care of her health, no matter what happened. Thirza, abrupt and without tears, lightly kissed Nell’s cheek and remarked she presumed they would receive word from her once she was established. An onlooker without intimate knowledge might have assumed that Nell’s departure was of small consequence to her—except if that onlooker had chanced to catch a clear glimpse into her eyes. Lucy gave Nell a stiff kiss and managed to produce two neat, small tears; yet Robin, who had been weeping on the back porch step from the moment they left the table, declined to bid farewell whatsoever. Observing Nell approach him, he leaped up, rushed up the rear staircase, and concealed himself inside a clothes closet, refusing to emerge. label: History
value: Captain Saul operates the Seven Gulls Point lighthouse.
unit: Captain Saul, also known as Uncle Saul, welcomes Nell and Hugh to their new home and becomes a frequent presence in their lives, sharing stories of local history and his time at sea. Operating the Seven Gulls Point lighthouse, he hosts gatherings where he introduces neighbors and entertains visitors with his collection of sea curiosities. He attends Christmas dinner with Nell, Hugh, and other friends, engaging in lively debate, and welcomes the New Year at the lighthouse surrounded by companions. Later, Saul comforts Nell during her grief over the loss of her newborn daughter, Joyce, and entrusts her with the story of his own long-lost love, Margaret. When Adrian Treleaven visits Seven Gulls Point, Saul realizes Adrian is the grandson of Damaris Tremayne, lends him his personal life log, and agrees to let Adrian write a book based on his seafaring adventures and his lost Margaret. Saul later provides funds to Lorna Vane so she can travel to Montreal for surgery on her supposed brother Rufus. Following a Liberal political victory, he contemplates his own mortality, asking Nell to care for his cat, First Mate, after he passes away. After bestowing a heartfelt blessing on Adrian and Lorna upon their engagement, Saul receives the printed copy of his life story, celebrating its arrival with Nell and Lorna. The following morning, Hugh and Nell discover that Captain Saul has peacefully passed away at the lighthouse with his book open on his chest.
